transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Ukrainian officials say a vital satellite link has been restored to full functionality.
Ukraine uses it to stop incoming Russian missile and drone attacks.
NPR's Greg Myrie reports yesterday the Starlink system was nearly crippled.
Ukraine's defense ministry is saying that this satellite network is back and working
as normal.
And by way of explanation, many people know the satellite communication system Starlink.
This is part of Elon Musk's empire.
But there's also a military version called Star Shield that he built for the U.S. government
and military.
The Pentagon shares this with Ukraine, which uses it to guide its drones.
But yesterday, Ukraine discovered quite abruptly that the Star Shield system had suddenly been
greatly restricted.
NPR's Greg Myrie reporting.
Family members of Minnesota Democratic Congresswoman Ilhan Omar are being subpoenaed.
That's as part of a federal investigation, including a search of Omar's Washington, D.C.
home.
NPR's Luke Garrett has more.
Immigration agents searched Omar's D.C. home one day.
The Justice Department said it was part of a federal criminal investigation.
According to an official familiar with but not authorized to share details on the case,
the probe has now expanded with subpoenas issued to members of the Congresswoman's family.
A separate source familiar with the case but not allowed to share details publicly tells
NPR the Omar investigation centers on immigration fraud allegations.
Omar has long denied these claims.
She is called to search on her home political targeting and a weaponization of federal law
enforcement.
The probe on the sitting member of Congress and candidate comes within just a few weeks
of the midterm elections, a break with the DOJ's 60-day rule.
This norm is meant to protect elections from politically motivated law enforcement.
Luke Garrett, NPR News, Washington.
We're learning more about the circumstances surrounding Christa Pike's failed execution
attempt in Tennessee last month.
Pike survived two rounds of lethal injections, but it was 90 minutes before she was taken
to the hospital.
Some 911 recordings of that night are surfacing.
From member station WPLN, Catherine Sweeney has more.
No one has ever survived two rounds of lethal injection drugs, so Tennessee's execution
protocols had no guidance.
Recordings obtained by WPLN depict a communication breakdown that found dispatchers trying to
figure out if requests for help were prank calls.
Prison workers denied needing medical help several times, even after an ambulance, fire
trucks and police escorts were sent out.
Here's a short exchange.
We have responders that are standing by, and we're just trying to verify.
I'm being told that nobody from our facility called you.
Pike was eventually taken to a hospital and has since been released back to prison.
For NPR News, I'm Catherine Sweeney in Nashville.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
A new survey finds more than four in 10 Americans had difficulty paying for at least one basic
necessity over the past year.
NPR's Jennifer Ludden reports it comes as the cost of living is a top election issue
for voters.
Paying for medical care was the biggest challenge people faced, including for more than a quarter
of middle income households.
That's according to a survey by the Pew Research Center.
Next was daily transportation, housing and food.
Only a third who struggled to pay for these things said they'd taken it alone.
Even more borrowed money from friends and family.
Pew also finds more than half of Americans did not have enough emergency savings to cover
expenses for three months.
The findings come amid stubborn inflation, with prices climbing faster than most people's
paychecks driven in part by the war with Iran.
Jennifer Ludden, NPR News, Washington.
Officials in Saudi Arabia say the headquarters of the country's oil company Aramco have been
hit.
Saudi officials are blaming Houthi rebels in neighboring Yemen.
The rebels say they have been firing into Saudi Arabia in retaliation for Saudi attacks
on them.
The Houthis have struck Saudi airports in recent days, killing and injuring scores of
people.
Archaeologists say they found the world's oldest shipwreck.
It is off the coast of Turkey.
It could be well over 4,000 years old.
Most of the structure of the ship is disintegrated, but searchers found clay jars that could have
held all of oil at one time.
Researchers will be able to learn more about ancient sailing customs.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Ukraine says its Starlink military satellite link is restored after nearly being crippled
Family members of Rep. Ilhan Omar subpoenaed in federal probe, including search of her D.C. home
Tennessee 911 recordings reveal confusion during Christa Pike's failed execution attempt
Pew survey finds over 40% of Americans struggled to pay for basic necessities last year
Saudi officials say Aramco headquarters hit, blaming Houthi rebels in Yemen
Archaeologists discover possibly 4,000-year-old shipwreck off the coast of Turkey
